S-2 CONFIRMED — the epoch save/restore is the right shape, in the right place, with the right unwind, and the interface is provably set-equal to the state it protects. `interface PackratEpoch` (packrat.ts:196-202) lists memo/heads/growing/lrStack/currentSrc; the module declares exactly those five globals (:133-135, :186, :193); packratEnter snapshots all five and installs empties (:218-230) and packratExit restores all five (:243-250). S-3 CONFIRMED — arming at construction rather than first invocation is the subtle, correct ordering, and it is a theorem rather than a race. `PACKRAT_ARMED = true` is the FIRST statement of makeMemoized (packrat.ts:290), before `p` is even bound at :292, and the reasoning at :146-155 is right: arming at first invocation would leave that invocation's own `packratEnter` (parser.ts:43) already returned unarmed, so the first memoized parse would run epoch-less. You cannot obtain a memoized parser without having armed. The one hole is the lazy back-edge (`Parser.lazy(() => memoize(...))`, lazy.ts:20-22), filed as C-15 and confirmed at MINOR — retention, not a wrong answer. It does not diminish the design.
